svg.title: Result: sleeve life, drift, sample
svg.text: MPX SPIN V1 (CONCEPT 04 DEVELOPED) · DESIGN REVIEW
Result 4 · Dirty water, light plastics and a sparse sample

text.tspan: Three effects that the flow numbers alone hide. Each one is a trade-off or a failure mode to carry forward.

svg.text: LITRES PER SLEEVE BEFORE THE CYCLE < 15 L/H

text.tspan: The cake of silt on the sleeve, not the microplastics, ends its life.
Tap water lasts 71 L; borewell water 18 L; turbid surface water
Silt resistance α = 10¹³ m/kg is assumed

svg.text: RADIAL DRIFT IN THE SPINNING WATER, 1,500 RPM

text.tspan: mm/s, + outward. The water itself moves outward through the
drift inward faster than that: they ride the inner
surface and only reach the sleeve as the last water drains, near its
top or on the floor. Dense PET and PVC are thrown onto the paper.

svg.text: MP-250 at 250×, 0.8 mm field, Nile red (simulated)

text.tspan: The sleeve is 188 × 180 mm: about 67,000 microscope fields.
One 400 mL batch at an assumed 1,000 particles per litre leaves
on one sleeve gives ≈ 0.3 per field; or cut and count
a small disc, or use a smaller sample sleeve.
Cellulose takes up Nile red: a
background, and cellulose fibres must not be counted as plastic.

svg.text: PD-298 · Team MPx · CPDM, IISc · Oct 2026
Drift: Stokes in a centrifugal field, v = Δρ d² ω² r / 18μ at r = 25 mm. Microscope: Carson MP-250, 250×, 0.8 mm field
